creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson (Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI)
description: XTREME-S (Cross-lingual Transfer Evaluation of Multilingual Encoders for Speech) is a benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations. It covers 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains, and 4 task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval. The benchmark includes datasets such as Fleurs, MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, and Minds-14, and introduces a new massively multilingual evaluation dataset called Fleurs in all 102 languages.

name: XTREME-S
rai:annotationsPerItem: Between 1 and 3 recordings per sentence (2.3 on average) for the Fleurs component of the benchmark.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: HuggingFace platform (datasets and fine-tuning scripts made accessible through HuggingFace)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For Fleurs, between one and three recordings were collected for each of the 2009 n-way parallel sentences (2.3 on average). Speakers of the train sets are different from speakers in the dev/test sets to avoid overfitting on speaker identity. For speech retrieval, the pool of transcription candidates is augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia per language.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark acknowledges a significant performance gap between Western European languages and other language groups (e.g., Sub-Saharan African, South Asian), which is partly explained by larger amounts of unlabeled data available for Western European languages in MLS and VoxPopuli. Reducing these gaps across geographical groups is identified as an important research direction. The benchmark was designed to cover diverse language families and geographical locations to mitigate geographic and linguistic bias in evaluation.
rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S is a benchmark that aggregates existing multilingual speech datasets (MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) and introduces a new dataset called Fleurs. Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark, using 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets in 102 languages. Between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence (2.3 on average), with new train-dev-test splits of 1509/150/350 sentences respectively. Training sets have around 10 hours of supervision, and speakers of the train sets are different from speakers in the dev/test sets.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark aggregates several existing datasets: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS, derived from Librivox audiobooks), VoxPopuli (European Parliament sessions), CoVoST-2 (speech translation corpus), and Minds-14 (e-banking spoken intent data). The new Fleurs dataset is built from 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets, covering 102 languages.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Results show significant performance gaps between language groups: Western European languages achieve much better results (e.g., 11.5 average WER) compared to Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7 average WER) languages, partly due to larger amounts of unlabeled data available for Western European languages. The benchmark focuses on linguistic aspects of speech and does not evaluate nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects relevant to speech synthesis or voice conversion. The Fleurs dataset is noted to be complete at more than 97%, with some slight improvements possible in a second version (e.g., missing recordings or low-quality recordings).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits were built with 1509/150/350 sentences for train/dev/test respectively. Speakers of the train sets are different from speakers in the dev/test sets. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For VoxPopuli, only the 14 languages with more than 10 hours of data from the ASR task were used. For MLS, the official 10-hour splits were used to evaluate few-shot learning capabilities. Unit error rate (characters, signs) is used for Fleurs ASR evaluation.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The Fleurs dataset is noted to be complete at more than 97%, with some slight improvements and changes possible in a second version (e.g., missing recordings or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on the HuggingFace platform. The paper notes that additional test sets may be added in the future to confirm the generalization ability of submissions, and a submission form will be provided for leaderboard submissions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: XTREME-S aims to make speech technology available in all languages, giving speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster. The benchmark encourages data-efficient self-supervised representation learning to enable speech technology for low-resource languages.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations; benchmarking multilingual speech models on speech recognition (ASR), speech-to-text translation (ST), speech classification (language identification and intent classification), and speech retrieval tasks; catalyzing research in universal speech representation learning across 102 languages.
